recommendations.regimenLabel: IVIG or plasma exchange + airway support
steps: ADMIT to ICU; monitor FVC/NIF — intubate early for respiratory failure.
IVIG or plasma exchange for the crisis.
Identify and remove triggers (infection, aminoglycosides, beta-blockers, magnesium).
Hold/adjust pyridostigmine acutely (secretions); optimise immunotherapy (steroids ± steroid-sparing) once stabilising.
Steroids may transiently worsen weakness — start cautiously under specialist care.

drugRefs.why: First-line rapid-acting therapy for myasthenic crisis; alternative to plasma exchange with comparable efficacy. Plasma exchange (≈5 exchanges over ~10 days) is the equivalent non-pharmacological option.

refs: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22e — Myasthenia Gravis and Other Diseases of the Neuromuscular Junction (Ch. 459)
International Consensus Guidance for Management of Myasthenia Gravis (Sanders et al., updated 2020)

drugRefs.dose: 1 mg/kg/day once stabilising; consider gradual up-titration to avoid early steroid-induced worsening
drugRefs.why: Mainstay maintenance immunotherapy, but high-dose steroids can transiently worsen weakness at initiation — introduce cautiously in an inpatient/ICU setting, ideally after IVIG/plasma exchange.

drugRefs.dose: 60 mg PO 3–4 times daily when used; commonly withheld or reduced acutely in crisis
drugRefs.why: Symptomatic only; often held during crisis to reduce airway secretions and because it does not treat the underlying process. Avoid escalating doses (risk of cholinergic crisis).

refs: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22e — Myasthenia Gravis and Other Diseases of the Neuromuscular Junction (Ch. 459)
International Consensus Guidance for Management of Myasthenia Gravis (Sanders et al., updated 2020)

confirm: Worsening bulbar/respiratory weakness in myasthenia gravis (or new presentation) with respiratory failure; often triggered by infection/drugs.
